sections.h2: Landscape design that starts with the plants, not the paving
sections.html:
Most landscape design in Adelaide starts with hard surfaces and fills the gaps with whatever the nursery has on special. I work the other way around. As a qualified horticulturist (Certificate III, and currently studying garden design), I begin with your soil, your aspect and how you actually use the yard, then build a planting plan that will still look right in five years. Hardscaping is brought in where it earns its place.

That approach suits the character homes of Burnside, Toorak Gardens, Rose Park and Kensington Park, where a garden has to sit comfortably against a bluestone villa or a 1920s bungalow, and it suits new builds in Magill and Campbelltown that need structure from day one.

sections.h2: Garden design Adelaide homeowners can live with
sections.html:
A good garden design for Adelaide has to survive 40-degree January days on tank water and a wet, cold July on heavy clay. I lean on plants that do both: Westringia, Correa and Lomandra for structure, Salvias and Kangaroo Paw for colour, and productive trees where there is room. If you want a native garden design for bees and birds, a Mediterranean courtyard, or a cottage-style front yard that still looks tidy in autumn, the plan is drawn around that.

  • On-site consultation and site assessment (sun, drainage, soil, existing trees)
  • Planting plan with plant list, quantities and positions
  • Softscaping: bed preparation, soil improvement, planting, mulching and edging
  • Hedge and screening installation
  • Drip irrigation design and installation so the new garden establishes properly
  • Staged plans if you would rather build the garden over a couple of seasons

sections.h2: Softscaping, done properly
sections.html:
Softscaping is the living half of landscaping: soil, plants, mulch and water. It is also where most Adelaide gardens fail, usually because the soil was never improved and the irrigation was never finished. On every job I condition the beds with compost and gypsum where the clay needs it, plant at the right depth and spacing, mulch to the right thickness, and run a drip line before the plants go in, not after.

I also install and repair irrigation as a service on its own, and most new gardens get a timer so the first summer is not left to chance.

sections.h2: What happens at a design consultation
sections.html: The first visit is a walk around the garden with a notebook, not a sales pitch. I look at where the sun falls in summer and winter, where water pools after rain, what the soil does when you dig a spade in, which existing plants are worth keeping and which are quietly dying. We talk about how you use the space: kids, dogs, entertaining, vegetables, privacy from the neighbours, how much time you honestly want to spend maintaining it. From that I draw a planting plan to scale, with a plant list you can take to a nursery or have me supply and plant. Most eastern-suburbs gardens are done in one or two stages, beds first and lawn or irrigation next, so the budget is spread and nothing is planted in the wrong season.

sections.h2: Where I design and build gardens
sections.html: Garden Grit is based in Norwood and travels up to 20 km, which covers Burnside, Toorak Gardens, Rose Park, Kensington Park, Magill, St Peters, Walkerville and the rest of Adelaide's eastern and north-eastern suburbs. Smaller design jobs, such as a single front bed or a courtyard refresh, are welcome.

faqs.q: How much does landscaping cost in Adelaide's eastern suburbs?
faqs.a: It depends on the size of the garden and how much hard landscaping is involved. A planting plan and softscaping for a typical suburban front or back yard is far cheaper than a full hard-landscape rebuild. I quote every job after a site visit, so you get a fixed price for the scope we agree on, with no hourly surprises.

faqs.q: Do you do garden design as well as the planting?
faqs.a: Yes. Many clients want the design and the installation done by the same person so nothing is lost between a drawing and the real garden. I can also supply a planting plan on its own if you want to do the planting yourself.

faqs.q: Can you design a native or low-water garden?
faqs.a: Native and low-water gardens are a specialty. Adelaide's climate suits a huge range of Australian natives and Mediterranean plants, and a well-planned native garden needs a fraction of the water of a lawn once it is established.

faqs.q: Do you do hard landscaping like paving and retaining walls?
faqs.a: My work is design and softscaping: soil, plants, mulch, edging, hedges and irrigation. For paving, decks or large retaining walls I work alongside trades I trust and can coordinate the sequence so the planting happens at the right time.

faqs.q: Which suburbs do you cover for landscape design?
faqs.a: Norwood and everywhere within about 20 km: Burnside, Toorak Gardens, Rose Park, Kensington Park, Magill, Campbelltown, Walkerville, Prospect, Bowden and up to Tea Tree Gully.

sections.h2: Garden maintenance by someone who knows what the plants need
sections.html:
There is a difference between a garden that has been tidied and a garden that has been maintained. Anyone can blow the leaves off a path. Knowing that your roses want a hard winter prune, your Lilly Pilly hedge should be shaped after the new flush, and that the yellowing on the citrus is a magnesium problem rather than a watering one is what a qualified horticulturist brings to garden maintenance in Adelaide.

I have been maintaining gardens in Norwood and the eastern suburbs since 2017. Most of my regular clients are busy households, retirees who want to keep the garden they love, and landlords who need a rental presented well between tenants.

sections.h2: Gardening services Adelaide homes and small businesses rely on
sections.html:
• Pruning of shrubs, roses, fruit trees and ornamentals at the right time of year
  • Weeding, bed edging and mulching
  • Lawn mowing, edging and seasonal lawn care for regular clients
  • Plant health, soil health and pest treatment
  • Planting replacements and seasonal colour
  • Gutter cleaning, pressure washing and the odd jobs that go with a tidy property

Regular maintenance can be fortnightly, monthly or seasonal. Most eastern-suburbs gardens need a heavier visit in late winter and late autumn, with lighter visits between.

sections.h2: Garden clean up Adelaide: residential and commercial
sections.html:
A garden clean up is for the jobs that have got away: an overgrown rental between tenants, a deceased estate being prepared for sale, a backyard that has not been touched since last spring, or a commercial site that needs to look presentable again. I clear, prune, weed, mulch and remove the green waste, and leave you with a garden you can actually maintain.

For commercial clean ups, body corporates and small business premises in Norwood, Kent Town, Stepney and St Peters, I can quote a one-off reset and then a maintenance schedule so it stays that way.

sections.h2: What a regular maintenance visit covers
sections.html:
A typical visit starts with a walk through to see what has changed since last time: new weeds, a shrub that has outgrown its spot, a lawn patch that is struggling, a drip line that has stopped. Then the work is prioritised by season. In spring that is pruning spring-flowering shrubs after they finish, feeding, mulching before the heat and getting the irrigation running. In summer it is keeping water up to the plants that need it, deadheading and light pruning only. In autumn it is the big tidy: leaf drop, cutting back perennials, planting, and preparing beds. In winter it is the hard pruning of roses, fruit trees and deciduous shrubs, and bare-rooted planting. You get a short note after each visit on what was done and what to watch.

Rental properties and strata sites get a simpler schedule: a presentable, safe, tidy garden on a fixed day each month, with photos sent to the property manager if required.

sections.h2: Suburbs covered for garden maintenance
sections.html: I am based in Norwood, so Kensington Park, St Peters, Stepney, Kent Town, Rose Park, Walkerville and Payneham are all a few minutes away. Regular maintenance runs extend across the whole service area, from Burnside to Prospect and out to Tea Tree Gully.

faqs.q: Do you do garden maintenance and clean ups in Norwood and Kensington Park?
faqs.a: Yes. Norwood is home base, and Kensington Park, St Peters, Stepney and Kent Town are my closest regular runs. One-off clean ups and ongoing maintenance are both available.

faqs.q: How often should a garden be maintained?
faqs.a: For most established eastern-suburbs gardens, a monthly visit keeps on top of pruning, weeds and mulch, with heavier work in late winter and autumn. Low-maintenance native gardens can go quarterly. Lawns and hedges in growing season need more frequent attention.

faqs.q: Do you take the green waste away?
faqs.a: Yes. Clean ups include removal of the prunings, weeds and debris unless you would rather keep material for compost or mulch.

faqs.q: Do you do commercial garden clean ups?
faqs.a: Yes. I take on small commercial sites, rental properties and body corporate grounds across Norwood and the eastern suburbs, as a one-off clean up or on a maintenance schedule.

faqs.q: Can you look after the lawn as well?
faqs.a: For regular maintenance clients I include mowing, edging and seasonal lawn care such as fertilising, coring and weed control, so the whole garden is looked after by the same person.

sections.h2: Hedge trimming Adelaide gardens actually look better for
sections.html: A hedge cut square and level is a simple thing that is surprisingly rare. It takes a string line, a steady hand and some knowledge of how each species regrows. A Lilly Pilly or Viburnum will take a hard cut and bounce back; a Conifer or a Lavender hedge cut into old wood will not recover. As a qualified horticulturist, I trim with the plant's growth habit and flowering time in mind, so the hedge gets tighter and healthier each season rather than thinner.

sections.h2: What is included in a hedge trim
sections.html:
• Formal hedges trimmed level and plumb with a string line, faces tapered so light reaches the base
  • Informal and screening hedges shaped to keep them dense and within bounds
  • Rejuvenation pruning for overgrown or leggy hedges, staged over a season or two where needed
  • Topiary balls, cloud pruning and feature plants
  • All clippings raked, blown and removed

Common hedges in the eastern suburbs include Lilly Pilly (Syzygium), Photinia, Viburnum, Murraya, Buxus, Pittosporum and Westringia. Each has a best time to cut and a limit to how hard it can be cut, and I will tell you which applies to yours.

sections.h2: Hedge pruning for homes, strata and body corporates
sections.html: The long boundary hedges of Walkerville, Prospect, Medindie and Toorak Gardens are a big part of those streets' character. I handle single-home hedges and the shared hedges, screens and street frontages that strata groups and body corporates in Norwood, Kent Town and St Peters need kept presentable, on a regular schedule if you prefer.

sections.h2: Why the first cut after a long gap is different
sections.html:
If a hedge has not been trimmed for a year or more, the first visit is about restoring the shape rather than just removing the fluff. That means finding the original line, cutting back to it in stages so the hedge is never stripped bare, and feeding and watering afterwards so it refills quickly. The second and third trims that year are quick, and by the following season the hedge is back on a normal schedule. I will tell you at the quote which category your hedge is in.

Hedges along driveways and footpaths in Norwood, Walkerville and Prospect also have a sight-line and council-clearance side to them. Keeping the hedge back from the footpath and below the height that blocks a driver's view is part of the trim, not an extra.

sections.h2: How often should a hedge be trimmed?
sections.html: In Adelaide's climate, most formal hedges want two or three trims a year: one in late winter before the spring flush, one in early summer, and often a tidy-up in autumn. Fast growers like Photinia and Lilly Pilly can take a fourth. I cover the reasoning in how often to trim a hedge in Adelaide's climate.

faqs.q: How often should hedges be trimmed in Adelaide's climate?
faqs.a: Two to three times a year for most formal hedges: late winter, early summer and an autumn tidy. Fast-growing hedges such as Photinia or Lilly Pilly may need four. Flowering hedges are trimmed straight after flowering so you do not lose next year's display.

faqs.q: Can you bring an overgrown hedge back under control?
faqs.a: Usually, yes. Most broadleaf hedges can be cut back hard and will regrow, though it is often staged over two seasons so the hedge never looks bare. Conifers and some others cannot be cut into old wood, so I will tell you honestly what is possible.

faqs.q: Do you trim tall hedges?
faqs.a: Yes, hedges up to a safe working height from a platform or ladder. Very tall screening trees are treated as tree pruning rather than hedging.

faqs.q: Do you take the clippings away?
faqs.a: Yes. Every hedge trim includes clean up and removal of the clippings.

faqs.q: Which suburbs do you cover for hedge trimming?
faqs.a: Norwood and the eastern suburbs, including Walkerville, Prospect, Toorak Gardens, Burnside, Magill, St Peters and north to Tea Tree Gully.

metaDescription: Tree pruning Adelaide by a qualified horticulturist: fruit trees, ornamentals and small trees pruned, not lopped. Magill, Campbelltown and the east.

sections.h2: Tree pruning Adelaide homeowners can trust: pruning, not lopping
sections.html: Lopping is cutting a tree back to stubs to make it smaller. It looks tidy for a month and then produces a thicket of weak, fast regrowth that is worse than what you started with. Proper tree pruning removes the right branches, at the right point, at the right time of year, so the tree stays strong, lets light into the garden and keeps a natural shape. That is the difference a qualified horticulturist makes.

sections.h2: What I prune
sections.html:
• Fruit trees: apples, pears, plums, apricots, citrus, figs and olives, pruned for fruit and for picking height
  • Ornamental trees: Crepe Myrtles, Japanese Maples, Magnolias, Robinias, Prunus and flowering fruit trees
  • Formative pruning of young trees so they develop a sound structure
  • Crown lifting and thinning to let light into lawns and beds underneath
  • Deadwood removal, crossing branches and clearance from gutters, paths and fences
  • Small tree and shrub removal, and stump removal where access allows

Work is limited to small and medium trees that can be pruned safely from the ground or a ladder. Large trees, trees near power lines or anything needing a climber or a chipper are referred to a qualified arborist, and I will tell you up front if that is what your tree needs.

sections.h2: Tree trimming Adelaide: timing matters
sections.html: Deciduous fruit trees are pruned in winter when they are dormant; stone fruit are better done in late summer after harvest to avoid disease. Crepe Myrtles are cut in late winter, Magnolias straight after flowering, and citrus only lightly, after the frost risk has passed. If you are not sure when your tree should be cut, ask. I have written a month-by-month guide to pruning fruit trees in South Australia.

sections.h2: What to expect on the day
sections.html: I start by walking around the tree and explaining which cuts I plan to make and why: a crossing branch here, a water shoot there, lifting the lower limbs so you can mow underneath. Cuts are made just outside the branch collar so the tree can seal them, never flush and never left as stubs. Large reductions are spread over more than one season so the tree is not shocked into a flush of weak regrowth. Everything is raked up and taken away, and if the tree had disease, the tools are sterilised between trees so it does not travel through your garden. For fruit trees you also get a quick word on feeding and watering so the pruning actually turns into fruit.

sections.h2: Suburbs covered for tree pruning
sections.html: The older gardens of Magill, Campbelltown, Athelstone, Paradise and Dernancourt are full of mature fruit and ornamental trees, and that is where most of my pruning work is. I also cover Norwood, Burnside and the rest of the eastern and north-eastern suburbs. See what moves the price of tree pruning in Adelaide before you book.

faqs.q: How much does tree pruning cost in Adelaide?
faqs.a: Small ornamental and fruit tree pruning is quoted per tree or per visit after I have seen the tree. Size, access, how long since it was last pruned and how much green waste there is to remove are what move the price. Every job is a fixed quote, not an hourly guess.

faqs.q: When is the best time to prune fruit trees in Adelaide?
faqs.a: Pome fruit (apples, pears) in winter while dormant; stone fruit (apricots, plums, peaches) in late summer after fruiting, to reduce disease; citrus lightly in spring after the last frost. Evergreen ornamentals can usually be pruned in late winter or after flowering.

faqs.q: Do you remove trees?
faqs.a: Small trees and shrubs, yes, including stump removal where access allows. Large tree removal is arborist work, and some trees in South Australia are protected under the Planning, Development and Infrastructure Act, so always check before removing a significant tree.

faqs.q: Will pruning make my tree smaller?
faqs.a: Pruning can reduce size gradually and keep a tree in proportion, but a tree cannot be made permanently small by cutting it back hard. If a tree is simply too big for its spot, I will say so and talk through options.

faqs.q: Do you work in Magill, Campbelltown and Athelstone?
faqs.a: Yes. Those north-eastern suburbs are a regular run from Norwood, along with Paradise, Dernancourt, Modbury and Tea Tree Gully.

title: Turf Installation & Lawn Laying Adelaide | Garden Grit
metaDescription: Turf installation Adelaide: soil prep, levelling, irrigation and roll-on lawn by a horticulturist in Tea Tree Gully, Modbury, Golden Grove and the east.
card: Soil prep, levelling, irrigation and roll-on lawn that establishes properly.

sections.h2: Turf installation Adelaide lawns need to survive summer
sections.html: Roll-on turf is the easy part of a new lawn. Whether it is still green in February comes down to what is underneath it: how the old surface was removed, how deep the soil was prepared, whether it was levelled with a fall away from the house, and whether water gets to the roots evenly. I prepare lawns the way a horticulturist prepares a garden bed, because that is what a lawn is.

sections.h2: How I lay a new lawn
sections.html:
1. Site assessment. Sun, shade, traffic and drainage decide which turf variety suits, and whether the area should be lawn at all.
  2. Removal and preparation. Old lawn, weeds and builders' rubble removed, soil loosened and improved with a quality sandy loam and organic matter.
  3. Levelling. Graded with a gentle fall away from buildings, compacted lightly and raked to a fine finish.
  4. Irrigation. Pop-up sprinklers or drip under the turf, installed before the rolls go down.
  5. Laying. Rolls laid brickwork-fashion, tightly butted, edges trimmed, then rolled and watered in.
  6. Aftercare plan. A written watering and mowing schedule for the first six weeks.

sections.h2: Which turf for Adelaide? Kikuyu, Buffalo and Couch
sections.html: For a full-sun family lawn in Modbury or Golden Grove, Kikuyu is hard to beat for price and toughness. Soft-leaf Buffalo handles the part-shade of established eastern-suburbs gardens far better and stays greener in winter. Couch varieties give a fine, tight surface for a show lawn but want full sun and regular care. I will recommend the variety that suits your site and your budget, and I cover the costs in lawn installation cost in Adelaide: Kikuyu, Buffalo and Couch compared.

sections.h2: Looking after a new lawn in the first six weeks
sections.html:
The six weeks after laying decide whether the lawn knits in or fails. For the first week the turf is watered every day, early morning, enough to soak through the rolls into the soil beneath; in summer that can mean twice a day. From week two the watering is stretched out so the roots chase the moisture down. Keep off the lawn as much as possible until it cannot be lifted at the corners, then do the first mow on a high setting with sharp blades. A light feed at around six weeks and the lawn is established. I leave every turf client with this schedule in writing, adjusted for the time of year and the irrigation that has been installed.

If a lawn already exists but is patchy, compacted or full of weeds, renovation (coring, dethatching, top dressing and overseeding or re-turfing the worst sections) can be cheaper than a full replacement. I will tell you which makes sense for yours.

sections.h2: Where I install turf
sections.html: Tea Tree Gully, Modbury, Golden Grove and the new-build suburbs of the north-east are regular turf jobs, as are renovations in Norwood, Magill and Campbelltown and lawn replacements for rentals and B&Bs across the eastern suburbs.

faqs.q: Can you install new turf in Tea Tree Gully, Modbury and Golden Grove?
faqs.a: Yes. The north-eastern suburbs are within my 20 km service area from Norwood and are some of the most common areas for new lawns, especially on new builds and renovations.

faqs.q: How much does lawn installation cost in Adelaide?
faqs.a: The turf itself is only part of the cost; preparation, soil, levelling and irrigation make up the rest. Buffalo costs more per square metre than Kikuyu, and a site that needs old lawn or rubble removed costs more to prepare. I quote after a site visit so the price covers everything the lawn needs to establish.

faqs.q: What is the best time of year to lay turf in Adelaide?
faqs.a: Spring and autumn are ideal: warm soil, mild air and some rain. Turf can be laid in summer with diligent watering, and in winter it establishes slowly. I avoid laying during heatwaves.

faqs.q: How long until I can walk on a new lawn?
faqs.a: Keep off it for about two to three weeks while the roots knit into the soil, then start light use. The first mow is usually at three to four weeks, once the turf cannot be lifted at the corners.

faqs.q: Do you install irrigation with the lawn?
faqs.a: Yes, and I recommend it. Pop-ups or sub-surface drip go in before the turf, so the lawn is watered evenly from day one and you are not dragging a hose around in January.

sections.h2: Irrigation installation Adelaide gardens are designed around
sections.html: Irrigation is not a plumbing job to me; it is the thing that decides whether the plants live. As a horticulturist I design the system around what is planted: drip lines with the right emitter spacing for garden beds, pop-ups for lawn, separate zones for pots, natives and thirsty vegetables, and a timer programmed for Adelaide's seasons and watering rules. That is why most of my landscape design and turf clients have the irrigation installed as part of the job.

sections.h2: Systems installed and repaired
sections.html:
• Drip irrigation for garden beds, hedges, vegetable patches and pots
  • Pop-up sprinkler zones for lawns
  • Tap timers and multi-zone controllers, including programming and seasonal adjustment
  • Repairs: blockages, leaks, split poly pipe, failed solenoids, broken pop-ups and missing emitters
  • Converting old spray systems to efficient drip
  • Flushing, pressure testing and a seasonal check-over for existing systems

sections.h2: Repairing a failing drip system
sections.html: A lot of eastern-suburbs gardens have a drip system that was installed years ago and slowly stopped working: emitters clogged with Adelaide's hard water, a line cut by a spade, a timer nobody has reprogrammed since it was fitted. Often the fix is an afternoon's work rather than a new system. I diagnose first and only replace what has actually failed.

sections.h2: Designing zones that match the garden
sections.html: The most common mistake in Adelaide irrigation is one zone for everything: the lawn, the hedge, the natives and the vegetable patch all on the same timer, so something is always too wet or too dry. A proper design separates plants with different needs. Lawns get pop-ups on their own station, hedges and screening plants get a drip line with closer emitters, natives get a sparse line that runs less often once they are established, and pots and vegetables get their own frequent, short cycle. Each zone is sized to the water pressure available at your tap so the last emitter on the line gets as much as the first.

sections.h2: Watering rules and timers
sections.html: South Australia's permanent water-wise measures mean sprinklers on lawns and gardens are watered outside the hottest part of the day, and drip systems are the efficient way to stay within the rules while keeping plants alive through summer. I program the controller for the season, show you how to change it, and include a note on how long each zone should run in spring, summer and autumn. A seasonal check-over, flushing lines and replacing tired emitters, keeps the system reliable for years.

sections.h2: Where I install irrigation
sections.html: From Norwood I cover Bowden, Payneham, Glynde, St Peters, Walkerville and Prospect to the north and west, and Burnside, Magill and Campbelltown to the east. The full service area runs up to Tea Tree Gully.

faqs.q: How much does irrigation installation cost in Adelaide?
faqs.a: A drip system for a few garden beds with a tap timer is a modest job; a multi-zone controller with lawn pop-ups and separate bed zones costs more. I quote after seeing the garden and your water supply, and repairs are quoted separately from new installs.

faqs.q: Is drip irrigation better than sprinklers?
faqs.a: For garden beds, yes: drip puts water at the roots, loses almost nothing to evaporation and keeps foliage dry, which means fewer fungal problems. Pop-up sprinklers are still the right choice for lawns.

faqs.q: Can you fix my existing watering system?
faqs.a: Yes. Blockages, leaks, broken pop-ups, dead solenoids and timers that will not hold a program are the most common repairs. Many systems only need a service rather than replacement.

faqs.q: Do you need a plumber for irrigation?
faqs.a: Garden irrigation connected at the tap with a backflow device does not need a plumber. Anything that involves the mains connection or a new tap does, and I can arrange that.

faqs.q: Do you install irrigation in Bowden and Payneham?
faqs.a: Yes, along with the rest of the inner east and north-east within about 20 km of Norwood.
